subject: Human Evolution
title: What We Still Don't Know
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What We Still Don't Know.

hook.text: After 160 years of fossil hunting, the family tree still has more gaps than branches.

buildup.text: Entire species remain known from a single jawbone or tooth. One new find can redraw everything.

discovery.text: We don't know exactly when or how language, art, or symbolic thought first appeared—or why.

twist.text: Vast regions—central Africa, Southeast Asia's jungles—are almost completely unexplored for fossils.

climax.text: The next great discovery could come tomorrow, from a cave, a desert, or a construction site.

punchline.text: Every answer digs up more questions.

quiz.question: Why does the human family tree still have many gaps?
options: Fossilization is rare and many regions are unexplored
